t.4.5.1: Then Hanumān, having gone from Ṛśyamūka to that Malaya mountain, told the king of the monkeys about the two heroic Rāghavas.
t.4.5.2: This is Rāma, of great wisdom and firm valor, who has arrived together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa; this Rāma is truly valiant.
t.4.5.3: Born in the family of the Ikṣvākus, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, is renowned as devoted to dharma and is the keeper of his father's command.
t.4.5.4: While this great-souled one, self-restrained, was dwelling in the forest, his wife was carried off by a demon; he has come to you for refuge.
t.4.5.6: This Rāma, the son of him by whom the earth was protected through austerity and truthful speech, has come to you for refuge on account of a woman.
t.4.5.5: He by whom the sacred fire was gratified with Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, and by whom sacrificial fees were likewise bestowed, cows given away by the hundreds of thousands.
t.4.5.7: These two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, desire friendship with you. Receive them and honor them, for both are most worthy of worship.
t.4.5.8: Having heard the words of Hanumān, Sugrīva, his heart gladdened and his anxiety gone, cast off the terrible fear he had felt of Rāghava.
t.4.5.9: Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, having assumed a human form and become most handsome to behold, spoke affectionately to Rāghava.
t.4.5.10: You are disciplined in dharma, valorous, and affectionate toward all; your virtues have been truly described to me by the son of Vāyu.
t.4.5.11: That you desire friendship with me, a vānara, is indeed an honour to me and truly the highest gain, O lord.
t.4.5.12: If friendship pleases you, here is my arm stretched out. Let hand be clasped with hand, and let a firm bond of covenant be made.
t.4.5.13: Hearing these well-spoken words of Sugrīva, he, his heart filled with delight, pressed Sugrīva's hand with his own; and, embracing a heartfelt friendship, he clasped the afflicted one in his arms.
t.4.5.14: Then Hanūmān, the subduer of foes, casting off the guise of a mendicant, in his own form kindled a fire between two pieces of wood.
t.4.5.16: Then the two of them, Sugrīva and Rāghava, walked around the blazing fire, keeping it on their right, and so entered into friendship.
t.4.5.15: Then, having worshipped the blazing fire with flowers and duly honoured it, he, greatly pleased and fully composed, set it down between the two of them.
t.4.5.17: Then the two of them, the monkey and Rāghava, their hearts filled with great joy, gazed at each other and could not have their fill of it.
t.4.5.18: Then the radiant Sugrīva, with undivided mind, spoke these words to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who knew the meaning of all things.
